summary:
When a NASA mission ends, the astronauts come home—but the robots stay behind. From early lunar landers to modern Mars rovers, dozens of machines are still sitting silently in the dust of other worlds.

In our stop-motion film, we bring these forgotten explorers back to life. While human spaceflight usually steals the spotlight, it was often these small machines that went first, braving freezing nights and dust storms to map alien terrain and search for signs of water. Built and animated frame by frame, our video is a tribute to the overlooked hardware that quietly shaped space history—made to spark curiosity in viewers of all ages.The only AI thing in this project is the voice
details:
For our project, we made a stop-motion video about NASA’s old and modern rovers, probes, and robots. Using printed photos, a camera, and editing software, we show how these machines explore space and what equipment was left behind on the Moon and Mars.

Instead of making a standard presentation, we wanted to tell the history of space exploration in a way that is fun and easy to follow for all ages. As a team, we focused on picking the right missions, staying historically accurate, and reminding people that robotic explorers deserve just as much credit as astronauts.
